title: Tiny Parham's band and how Chicago clubs ran
summary: Parham was a fine pianist who wrote most of the tunes; clubs kept bands for long stays and all had shows.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, Tiny used to rehearse.
Tell me about Tiny Parham. He's sort of a mystery man to me. I don't know too much about him.
Yeah? Oh, yeah, he was a great musician. Heck of a piano player. He wrote all the tunes that we recorded; he wrote most of them.
Well, what kind of bands did he have?
Just about the same as Jelly's. Same instrumentation. Clarinet, trumpet, trombone, tuba.
Was he from New Orleans or Chicago?
You know, I don't know where Tiny was from. And you know that's Truck Parham's uncle.
It is?
Uh-huh.
I asked Truck about that one time and forgot what he said.
Well, that's what they tell me.
Well, was Tiny Parham pretty popular around Chicago?
Yeah.
Well, would the bands go from one club to another, or do they tend to settle in to one club, you know, like Reinhardt, or --
Yeah, they'd settle into one club. You didn't do too much jumping around, unless you got a notice or something, and then you started looking for another job.
Did all the clubs have shows?
Yeah. The smallest club had a show. Two, three girls, and two, three acts. Yeah.
Singers and dancers?
Singers and dancers.
And then the band just played for dancing?
Yeah.
And the show.
And the shows.
Did you get silly requests then, too?
Yeah.
What were some of the tunes that guys played back then?
You know, I can't remember. That's something -- that's been my problem, far as remembering tunes. Lot of times I'll play a tune and say, what the heck is the name of this tune? What am I playing now.
